chains.title: TCF7L2 binds the ref G allele more; risk allele T loses TCF7L2-mediated repression, increasing POU5F1B and CRC risk

links.claim: TCF7L2 is named as the candidate TF; QBiC-SELEX coverage is mapped, not own_model, through CIS-BP-mapped models of related HMG/Sox TFs (LEF1, TCF7, TCF7L1), and the passing mapped models predict ref G binds more strongly than alt T. ENCODE TCF7L2 ChIP-seq has a peak in HCT116 that contains the variant, supporting occupancy at this element, though not allele specificity.
The variant lies in the proximal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3858447 with DNase, H3K27ac, and CTCF signal.

POU5F1B is the strongest L2G gene at this locus and is a TWAS candidate functionally implicated in CRC growth and metastasis; TCF7L2 regulation of POU5F1B is proposed, not directly shown by these evidence IDs.
HCT116 is the provided DepMap expression context, and TCF7L2 ChIP-seq has a variant-containing peak in HCT116.
rs6983267 is strongly associated with colorectal cancer, with T reported as the CRC effect allele.

grades_v0.reason: E03 reports chromatin/cCRE overlap, not TCF7L2 binding. TCF7L2 is not in any provided QBiC-SELEX group row, and qbic_coverage is correctly left as not_checked, but no evidence supports the ref-G>alt-T TCF7L2 binding claim. TCF7L2 is also chosen without a QBiC-SELEX group or literature citation.
E01 places the variant in an Ensembl enhancer and E03 places it in pELS EH38E3858447 with DNase, H3K27ac, and CTCF signal.

E05 gives POU5F1B as the strongest L2G gene (0.89); E06b lists POU5F1B among TWAS candidate genes; E06c supports POU5F1B function in CRC proliferation/metastasis. This supports POU5F1B as an effector gene, not TCF7L2 regulation of it.
E07 states the DepMap expression context is ACH-000971, which the case identifies as HCT116. This supports the cell-type context claim, though not TCF7L2 expression.

E04 and E06a strongly support rs6983267 association with colorectal cancer. However, E04 reports the CRC effect allele as T, while H1 claims ref G increases CRC risk; this is a chain-level direction inconsistency.

E14 directly shows NR2F6 as an own-model passing member with z 20.82 and effect +1.92, i.e. the alt T allele is predicted to bind more in QBiC-SELEX. But this is an in vitro binding prediction only; no allele-specific ChIP, reporter, or other perturbation evidence is provided. NR2F6 selection is at least justified by passing status and 37.02 TPM.
E01/E03 support that the variant lies in pELS EH38E3858447.
E05/E06b/E06c support POU5F1B as the strongest L2G gene and as functionally implicated in CRC. They do not show that NR2F6 regulates POU5F1B, so the chain title's 'activates' is over-claimed.
E14 lists NR2F6 at 37.02 TPM and E07 identifies the expression context as ACH-000971/HCT116. This supports the expression-context claim.

E04/E06a support CRC association. The alt T allele is the reported CRC effect allele, which is direction-consistent with alt-T-enhanced NR2F6 binding only if NR2F6 truly activates POU5F1B; that activation is not evidenced.

E12 directly shows ZBTB43 as an own-model passing member with z -23.26 and effect -1.724, i.e. alt T binds less and ref G is predicted to bind more by QBiC-SELEX. This is an in vitro binding prediction only; no ChIP or allele-specific evidence. ZBTB43 selection is justified by own-model passing status and 8.32 TPM.
E01/E03 support that the variant lies in pELS EH38E3858447.
E05/E06b/E06c support POU5F1B as the strongest L2G gene and functionally implicated in CRC. They do not show ZBTB43 repression of POU5F1B, so the chain title's 'represses' is over-claimed.
E12 lists ZBTB43 at 8.32 TPM and E07 identifies the expression context as ACH-000971/HCT116. This supports the expression-context claim.
E04/E06a support CRC association. The chain does not explicitly state the risk-allele direction, and the ref-G-binding/repression model is not directly tested.

grades_final.reason: TCF7L2 coverage=mapped is shown in E18, but only via CIS-BP-mapped models of related HMG/Sox TFs (LEF1, TCF7, TCF7L1), not an own TCF7L2 model. In the post-GWAS analyses, we first identified new genome-wide significant associations: three genomic risk loci were identified at 8q24.21 (rs6983267, P = 6.98 × 10-12), 15q13.3 (rs58658771, P = 1.40 × 10-10), and 18q21.1 (rs6507874, P = 1.91 × 10-14).

In addition, the TWAS also identified four loci statistically significantly associated with CRC risk, largely explained by expression regulation, including six candidate genes (DUSP10, POU5F1B, C11orf53, COLCA1, COLCA2, and GREM1-AS1).
Correlating this observation, we demonstrate that POU5F1B fosters the proliferation and metastatic potential of CRC cells.

We further determine that POU5F1B, in spite of its phylogenetic relationship with the POU5F1/OCT4 transcription factor, is a membrane-enriched protein that associates with protein kinases and known targets or interactors as well as with cytoskeleton-related molecules, and induces intracellular signaling events and the release of trans-acting factors involved in cell growth and cell adhesion.
